rubric: Prioritize serious incorrect or unsafe contracts (S1), reader goal blockers (S2), missing topics (S3), then friction (S4); decisions below weigh concrete impact rather than voting min/max.

adjudications.rationale: Serious unsafe configuration contract: an integration intending field-only inspection can silently run TRUSTED inspection, which may invoke guest methods, with neither rejection nor a diagnostic identifying the fallback. The adjacent case-insensitive format/type-style handling increases the realistic chance of writing fields. This takes precedence over ordinary reader friction. Whole-job isolation remains mandatory; this finding does not claim FIELDS is a sandbox.

src/main/java/cs1302/tracer/internal/execution/TraceJob.java:164-165 resolves null inspection to TRUSTED unless multithread implies FIELDS.
Original independent reproduce vote records the lowercase fields case; this pass checked the current source statically and did not rerun it.
adjudications.fix_scope: Document exact uppercase enum tokens and the silent TRUSTED fallback; keep any Java validation change outside this documentation pass.
adjudications.verification: Current documentation/code source inspection plus preserved original independent evidence; no fresh runtime execution, build, or network lookup.

adjudications.rationale: The runner contract already names explicit finite values for all limits and directly links the complete bounded-tracing policy, which twice explains that omitted envelope limits are unlimited. It also requires independent whole-job CPU, memory, output and wall-clock enforcement. Tightening Prefer and repeating the default removes cross-page ambiguity, but the existing linked contract supplies the necessary rule. This is a minor consistency improvement, not an undocumented resource-isolation guarantee.

adjudications.rationale: Trusted batch users can obtain different results from the same source depending on previous jobs because reusing one JVM retains JDK-global state outside the documented job-owned data. This materially blocks reliable batch integration and needs a concrete reset/persistence contract and fresh-guest option. Downgrade from S1 because current batch and runner guidance already says class-loader separation is not OS isolation and requires one disposable tracer process per untrusted job; the docs do not explicitly promise that every JDK-global facility is reset.
current_static_evidence: docs/reference/batch.md:87-90 expressly describes reuse, while :95-98 warns that class-loader separation is not OS isolation and untrusted jobs require a disposable tracer process.
docs/tutorials/batch-jobs.md:56-60 scopes source/output/observations/snapshots per job, describes reuse, and links the one-process-per-untrusted-job rule.

src/main/java/cs1302/tracer/internal/guest/GuestHarness.java:208-211 creates a new job class loader, while :383-404 resets listed streams, properties, locale, time zone, handler and harness state, not arbitrary JDK-global static facilities.
Original independent reproduce vote records CookieHandler and logging state persisting across two jobs; this pass made only static checks.
adjudications.fix_scope: Document exactly which supported state is restored, which process/JDK-global state can persist, and the scope of maxJobsPerWorker(1). A fresh guest JVM does not undo filesystem changes. Do not edit App.java or its generated help in this pass.
adjudications.verification: Current documentation/code source inspection plus preserved original independent evidence; no fresh runtime execution, build, or network lookup.

adjudications.rationale: Silently ignored protection keys combined with unlimited omitted budgets form a serious unsafe configuration contract. The reference gives no complete JSON-key map, and timeoutMillis/snapshots cannot be derived reliably from --timeout-ms/--max-snapshots; a plausible request can therefore run without intended protection and without any diagnostic. The negative-limit null-id correlation behavior is an additional correctness issue. External whole-job controls remain mandatory, but they do not make the promised per-job budget configuration reliable.

src/main/java/cs1302/tracer/api/TraceLimits.java:25-26 defines all eleven actual record keys, and :53-56 rejects negative values.

src/main/java/cs1302/tracer/internal/batch/BatchTraceService.java:201-215 directly deserializes the request, catches constructor/parse failures before a request is returned and emits a null-id parse failure.

adjudications.fix_scope: Provide all eleven JSON limit names and units, explain unknown-key behavior, recommend checking echoed effective limits, and distinguish negative-limit parse_error/null-id responses. Keep parsing changes outside the documentation scope.

adjudications.rationale: The documented presentation goal cannot be achieved in modern output with this flag, yet the page uses modern in its recipes and describes inline-strings without a format qualification. This is a real behavior mismatch that wastes attempts and prevents the requested representation. It does not lose program data or silently weaken a safety setting, so S1 overstates its practical impact.
